 Volkswagen Recalls Over 610,000 Vehicles in China for Corroding Steering Gear Mounting Bolts
 Volkswagen's Chinese dealers will replace steering gear mounting bolts as part of a massive safety recall that covers domestic and imported vehicles 
 Published: 8 Nov 2026, 13:44 UTC 
 By: 
 Mircea Panait 
   47 photos Photo: Volkswagen 
 Europe's largest automaker is facing a pretty sizable recall in the world's largest new car market. Per a filing published by the Chinese State Administration for Market Regulation, the group is recalling an estimated 610,297 vehicles in the Middle Kingdom for a corrosion-related safety concern. 
 The Audi Q3 crossover accounts for the overwhelming majority of the affected population. All vehicles in this recall feature right steering gear mounting bolts that may corrode after prolonged exposure to moisture and de-icing agents. The weakened connection ultimately leads to a separation, and such failures understandably hinder steering performance.
 Volkswagen and its joint ventures with SAIC and FAW are instructing dealers to replace all suspect right-side bolts with an improved component. Free of charge, of course! The replacement bolts are said to feature a new corrosion-resistant polymer that should last a lot more than the recalled steering gear mounting bolts.
 Four individual campaigns include Volkswagen, SAIC Volkswagen, and FAW Volkswagen vehicles produced between September 2014 and September 2026. Said 12-year timeframe explains why more than 600,000 vehicles are potentially affected, with seven individual model lines accounting for 222,039 vehicles. The Q3, meanwhile, is listed with 388,258 units.
 Volkswagen (China) Sales handles all imported vehicles under campaign number S2026M0138V, covering Touareg sport utility vehicles and Golf compacts from September 2, 2014, through August 23, 2019. SAIC Volkswagen, meanwhile, has to fix 116,864 examples of the Teramont and 24,977 of the Teramont X.
 Photo: Volkswagen 
This joint venture further has to remedy 8,529 units of the Viloran, whereas the Audi brand adds 20,369 examples of the domestically produced Q6. This model should not be confused with the Q6 e-tron. The internal combustion Q6, which is produced in Zhejiang, is a full-size luxury crossover with the very same MQB Evo underpinnings as the Golf, Passat, Tiguan, Atlas, and Atlas Cross Sport.
 Regarding the joint venture with FAW, campaign number S2026M0140V covers the minivan-esque Talagon three-row sport utility vehicle, specifically models assembled from December 14, 2020, through July 8, 2022. Campaign S2026M0141V also comes from FAW Volkswagen, and it covers the domestically produced Q3 crossover.
 In all of these vehicles, the subject bolts may lose integrity, enabling the right-side steering gear connection to fail. While mounting bolts may sound particularly important, such failures definitely pose a safety risk. Volkswagen urges Chinese owners to immediately stop driving if they hear a metallic knock from the front axle. In this case, schedule a service appointment as soon as possible.
 There is, however, a problem with customers who hear this sound before January 2027. As it happens, all four distinct campaigns over the same issue carry a January 15, 2027, start date. The company will contact affected owners by SMS and registered mail in the meantime.
